Through the opinions of the line managers of staff members.
Through objective evidence of staff training, qualifications, skills, and experience.
Through the overall amount of time that an employee has worked for the organization.
feedbacks: Self assessments are subjective and not reliable.
Manager opinion is subjective.
Objective evidence is required to verify competency.
Tenure is not a reliable measure of competence.
questions.explanation: Competence is best verified by objective evidence of relevant training, skills, qualifications and experience.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what should be the primary focus of all ‘communication’ activities that relate to a QMS?
answers: To maintain complete secrecy about the operation of the QMS and to avoid sharing any information outside of the organization.
To ensure that only the management team are fully informed about the operation of the QMS.
To ensure that all relevant internal and external stakeholders receive all of the appropriate information about the QMS.
To keep all communications to a minimum, to prevent information overload amongst staff members.
feedbacks: Transparency and open communication is key.
Relevant information should be shared across all levels.
Sharing relevant information with all stakeholders is essential.
Communication must be effective and targeted.
questions.explanation: Communication should be targeted at all stakeholders with relevant information provided in an appropriate manner.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, which is NOT a typical requirement for the ‘control of documented information’?
answers: That all documentation must be stored in a single centralized physical location.
That documentation is kept up to date, with revisions regularly recorded.
That documentation must be protected from unauthorized access or alteration.
That documentation is readily available to all of those who require it.
feedbacks: A single location is not mandatory.
Regular reviews and updates are essential.
Protection from unauthorized access is essential.
Accessibility to those who need it is essential.
questions.explanation: Location of documentation is not specified, the key is accuracy, access and protection.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, what is the primary aim of implementing a ‘corrective action’?
answers: To ensure that those who are responsible for the nonconformity are suitably punished.
To resolve the immediate issue that has been identified but to take no further action to analyze the cause.
To conduct a full root cause analysis and to take actions that will prevent the nonconformity from happening again.
To document the nonconformity in order to satisfy any audit requirements.
feedbacks: Punishment is not the goal of corrective action.
Immediate correction is not enough to prevent reoccurrence.
Root cause analysis and preventative action is key.
Documentation is one aspect of the process.
questions.explanation: Corrective action is focused on root cause analysis and the implementation of preventative measures.

questions.question: When selecting an external provider, what is the MOST important factor to consider, according to ISO 9001:2025?
answers: The past relationship that the provider has had with your organization.
The brand recognition and popularity of the provider within the industry.
The providers ability to consistently meet all of your specified requirements.
The lowest overall cost that is offered by the external provider.
feedbacks: Past relationships should not be the only consideration.
Popularity is not a reliable measure.
Ability to consistently meet requirements is essential.
Cost should not be the only factor.
questions.explanation: External providers should be chosen on their proven ability to meet all of your organization's requirements.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the primary objective of ‘monitoring and measurement’ activities?
answers: To collect as much data as possible, whether or not the information is useful.
To ensure that processes are being followed exactly as they have been written.
To assess the performance of processes and to use this data to identify areas for improvement.
To ensure compliance with the standard and to satisfy any requirements of the external auditor.
feedbacks: Data collection must be targeted and relevant.
Following process without understanding effectiveness is not enough.
Performance assessment and driving improvement is the core objective.
Audit compliance is only one aspect of monitoring and measurement.
questions.explanation: Monitoring and measurement should be targeted at performance assessment and identifying areas for improvement.

questions.question: What does ISO 9001:2025 emphasize regarding the importance of ‘customer satisfaction’?
answers: That customer satisfaction is a lower priority than meeting internal targets and objectives.
That customers should be provided with products or services that meet only their minimum requirements.
That organizations must strive to understand their customers’ needs and expectations and then to exceed them wherever possible.
That the organization should establish processes and procedures that they can manage effectively and that the customer should adapt accordingly.
feedbacks: Customer satisfaction should be a high priority.
Meeting minimum requirements is not the objective.
Meeting and exceeding customer expectations is key to customer satisfaction.
Customer needs should drive process design.
questions.explanation: Customer satisfaction should be driven through a proactive approach that seeks to meet and exceed their expectations.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the overarching purpose of ‘continual improvement’?
answers: To maintain existing systems and processes at their current level and to avoid any change.
To make changes to the QMS to follow the latest trends regardless of their usefulness.
To ensure that the overall suitability, effectiveness and efficiency of the QMS is continuously improved.
To reduce documentation and administrative overhead, irrespective of the impact on overall quality.
feedbacks: Improvement requires change.
Changes must be relevant and targeted.
This is the main aim of continual improvement.
Cost reduction should not be prioritised over quality.
questions.explanation: Continual improvement is about ensuring the QMS becomes progressively more effective, efficient and suitable over time.

questions.question: When implementing changes to a QMS what is the MOST appropriate first step as required by ISO 9001:2025?
answers: To implement all changes immediately to realize any potential benefits quickly.
To carry out a full assessment of the potential risks and the impact that the changes will have on the QMS.
To create a comprehensive set of documentation that relates to the proposed changes.
To contact all external auditors to advise them of the changes that are proposed.
feedbacks: Changes must be planned not immediately actioned.
Risk and impact assessment is essential prior to making changes.
Documentation is an important part of the process but it is not the first step.
External auditors should be informed after the changes have been planned.
questions.explanation: Risk and impact assessment is essential to manage change effectively and to avoid negative outcomes.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, how should ‘documented information’ be managed within an organization?
answers: It should be stored in a single centralized location and all access to this should be tightly controlled.
It should be maintained solely by the quality manager, and they should be the only ones who have access to the records.
It should be protected from unauthorized access, kept up to date, and readily available to those who need it.
It should only be created when it is required for external audit purposes and not for operational use.
feedbacks: A single location is not mandatory and access should be available to those who need it.
Responsibility for documentation should be shared.
Accuracy, security and accessibility are essential.
Documentation should be a tool for effective QMS operation.
questions.explanation: Documented information should be accurate, accessible, and protected to ensure it can be used effectively.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the core responsibility of ‘leadership’ in relation to a QMS?
answers: To delegate all responsibility for the QMS to a specialist team of quality professionals.
To have no direct interaction with the QMS, and to allow operations to be managed by operational staff.
To actively engage with, support, promote, and maintain the QMS and its objectives.
To focus solely on the financial performance of the business and to ignore the activities of the QMS.
feedbacks: Delegation is not a complete abdication of responsibility.
Leaders must have a strategic overview of the QMS.
Active engagement with the QMS is essential for effective leadership.
QMS performance is linked to financial performance.
questions.explanation: Leadership is responsible for actively supporting, promoting and maintaining the QMS.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, how should ‘interested parties’ be identified and then considered within a QMS?
answers: As only those individuals who have a direct contractual relationship with the organization.
As only those individuals who are employed by the organization such as management and operational staff.
As any individual or group who is affected or perceives themselves to be affected by the activities of the organization.
As only those external organizations such as regulatory bodies who are involved in the QMS.
feedbacks: The definition is broader than just contractual relationships.
The definition is broader than just internal staff.
This provides a broad and accurate definition of interested parties.
The definition is broader than just external bodies.
questions.explanation: Interested parties include all those who are affected or feel they are affected by the operation of the organization.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically included in the ‘performance evaluation’ process according to ISO 9001:2025?
answers: The analysis of all data that has been collected from monitoring and measurement activities.
The evaluation of the effectiveness of corrective actions that have been implemented.
A comparison of the organizations performance against the performance of a similar business in a different sector.
The review of all feedback that has been received from customers and clients.
feedbacks: Data analysis is essential to performance evaluation.
Effectiveness of corrective actions is key to the evaluation process.
Benchmarking against non-competitors is not part of the evaluation.
Customer feedback is essential for effective performance evaluation.
questions.explanation: Performance evaluation is focused on internal processes and is not about benchmarking against organizations in other sectors.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the overall aim of ‘continual improvement’?
answers: To ensure that the existing QMS is maintained without making any unnecessary changes to processes.
To make changes to the system based on the latest industry trends, whether or not these are relevant or beneficial to the business.
To consistently improve the overall effectiveness, suitability and efficiency of the QMS over time.
To focus on administrative overhead and to make savings in costs, even if this results in a reduction in the quality of the service.
feedbacks: The emphasis is on improvement not maintaining the status quo.
Changes must be targeted and relevant to the business.
This is the main aim of continual improvement.
Cost cutting should not be at the expense of quality.
questions.explanation: Continual improvement is about making the QMS more efficient, effective and suitable over time.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, which element primarily focuses on proactively identifying potential risks and opportunities related to quality management objectives?
answers: Context of the organization
Leadership
Planning
Operation
feedbacks: This element helps in understanding the external and internal factors influencing the QMS, but doesn't directly identify risks.
Leadership establishes the vision and commitment but doesn't identify risks and opportunities directly.
Planning is where risks and opportunities are explicitly considered and actions are taken.
Operation deals with the actual activities of the QMS, not the initial assessment of risks and opportunities.
questions.explanation: The Planning section of ISO 9001:2025 requires the identification, consideration, and mitigation of risks and the pursuit of opportunities.

questions.question: A company implementing ISO 9001:2025 discovers a systemic issue in its supply chain that could lead to non-conforming products. Which approach aligns BEST with the standard's emphasis on continual improvement?
answers: Isolate the affected suppliers and source from new providers.
Document the non-conformance and correct the immediate batch of products.
Analyze the cause of the systemic issue and implement corrective actions throughout the supply chain.
Increase inspection frequency for products coming from the affected supplier(s).
feedbacks: While a mitigation strategy, it doesn't address the root cause of the issue within the supply chain.
Addresses the symptom but doesn't identify the systemic cause of the issue.
Corrective action addresses the root cause and is aligned with continual improvement.
This only serves as a control measure but is not a long term solution.
questions.explanation: Analyzing the systemic cause, and implementing corrective actions, is a key aspect of continual improvement in the context of the standard.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the primary purpose of the 'documented information' control mechanism?
answers: To generate excessive paperwork for audits.
To limit employee flexibility in executing processes.
To ensure process consistency, traceability, and evidence of conformity.
To primarily satisfy external auditors' demands.
feedbacks: The ISO 9001 standard aims for efficient processes, not just increasing paperwork.
The documentation is for consistency and best practices and should not limit flexibility.
Ensuring traceability, consistency, and providing evidence are core requirements of QMS documentation.
The documentation's main goal is to aid the QMS, not just to please auditors.
questions.explanation: Documented information within a QMS ensures process consistency and traceability and acts as proof of adherence to standards.

questions.question: In an organization, the management review process fails to effectively address performance data analysis. What’s the most likely impact concerning ISO 9001:2025 compliance?
answers: Enhanced employee engagement and participation.
Reduced risk of non-conformities and increased efficiency.
Decreased likelihood of achieving strategic goals.
Improved documentation and process controls.
feedbacks: Not directly related to a faulty management review.
An effective management review process helps minimize non-conformities.
Management review is essential to the organization's strategic goals.
Documentation and controls are separate from the management review effectiveness.
questions.explanation: If management review does not effectively analyze performance data, the organization's ability to set strategic goals and take strategic actions is hampered.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios demonstrates the BEST application of the 'risk-based thinking' approach in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Ignoring risks associated with a new process due to time constraints.
Treating all risks in the same way regardless of their severity or probability.
Establishing a system to identify, evaluate, and address risks and opportunities throughout the organization's processes.
Implementing a risk management system exclusively during the annual audit preparation.
feedbacks: Ignoring risks is not in line with the standards.
Effective risk management requires prioritization.
This represents the core element of risk-based thinking.
Risk management should be ongoing not just annual.
questions.explanation: Risk based thinking is about proactively addressing risks throughout the organization.

questions.question: What is the significance of defining 'context of the organization' in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: To create a checklist for legal compliance.
To determine the company's financial performance.
To understand external and internal issues impacting the organization's QMS and its strategic direction.
To establish the organization’s marketing strategies.
feedbacks: Context helps identify internal and external factors, not just legal aspects.
Context is important for understanding the company environment but isn’t about financials.
Context analysis ensures a quality system aligns with the organization's environment.
Context of the organisation is separate to marketing strategy.
questions.explanation: The context of an organization ensures the QMS is responsive and relevant by identifying internal and external influences that impact strategic direction.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, 'competence' of personnel is primarily verified through:
answers: Assessing the employee's willingness to learn new skills.
Evaluating the employee's social skills.
Demonstration of abilities, relevant education, and training records.
Reviewing the employee’s personal interests.
feedbacks: While important, willingness is not a full measure of competence.
Social skills are not directly related to competence.
Competence is verified through observable skills and proof of education and training.
Personal interests are not related to competency in the QMS.
questions.explanation: Competence refers to the demonstration of relevant skills and knowledge, backed by education and training records.

questions.question: A key change in ISO 9001:2025 from its previous version is the emphasis on:
answers: A focus on prescriptive procedures and documentation.
Eliminating the need for any documentation.
A more process-oriented approach, with increased emphasis on risk-based thinking and leadership engagement.
Rigid adherence to quality objectives, regardless of contextual changes.
feedbacks: The emphasis is now on the outcome of the system, not prescriptive rules.
Documentation is required, but there is more flexibility.
Process-orientation, risk-based thinking and leadership are at the core of the revised standard.
Rigid adherence would be counterproductive.
questions.explanation: ISO 9001:2025 focuses on performance, risk management and leadership commitment, rather than being prescriptive.

questions.question: A company has a complex supply chain with multiple sources for the same component. How should this variability in supply be addressed under ISO 9001:2025?
answers: By using only one supplier to reduce variability.
By only focusing on the supplier with the cheapest option.
By establishing documented criteria for supplier selection, evaluation and control of supplier performance.
By accepting variability in the component as an inherent risk.
feedbacks: This is not realistic and could increase risk.
Price should not be the only consideration.
Documented criteria for supplier selection ensures a systematic approach to variability.
This is an incorrect approach to risk management.
questions.explanation: Documented criteria for selection and performance management of suppliers is a best practice to manage supply variability and risk.

questions.question: What does the 'customer-focused' principle of ISO 9001:2025 primarily emphasize?
answers: Compliance with legal regulations and standards.
Achieving profit maximization, regardless of customer concerns.
Understanding and meeting customer requirements and exceeding customer expectations.
Developing generic products with wide appeal.
feedbacks: Legal compliance is not the main emphasis.
Profit maximization should be secondary to customer satisfaction.
This is the main focus of the customer-focused principle.
The focus is on customer requirements not generic products.
questions.explanation: The customer-focused principle underscores that understanding and meeting customers needs is key.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, what is the primary purpose of internal audits?
answers: To showcase the company’s accomplishments to external auditors.
To identify and correct non-conformities, and assess the effectiveness of the QMS.
To prepare documentation for external audit purposes.
To assign blame for system failures.
feedbacks: This is not the purpose of an internal audit.
This is the core aim of an internal audit.
The main focus is on internal improvement, not external preparation.
Audits are not about blaming individuals, they are about improving processes.
questions.explanation: Internal audits ensure that the QMS is functioning as intended by identifying non conformities and areas of improvement.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the role of 'Leadership' in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: To carry out administrative tasks related to the QMS.
To define and implement the quality policy and quality objectives.
To focus on operational tasks directly involved with quality.
To solely rely on external consultants for QMS guidance.
feedbacks: Leadership is more strategic than administrative.
This is a key role for leadership within the standards.
Operational tasks are not for leadership.
Reliance on external consultants alone is inadequate.
questions.explanation: Leadership is responsible for establishing and maintaining a quality policy and setting quality objectives for the QMS.

questions.question: In ISO 9001:2025, 'monitoring and measurement' of processes should be:
answers: Conducted sporadically as needed.
Focused only on final product output.
Consistent, and directly related to key performance indicators (KPIs).
Based solely on the number of customer complaints.
feedbacks: Monitoring and measurement should be consistent.
Monitoring must be process focused not just the outcome.
The monitoring of KPIs is essential for performance measurement.
Customer complaints are only one data point not the only one.
questions.explanation: Monitoring and measurement should be consistent and directly related to KPIs to maintain process consistency.

questions.question: A critical supplier of an organization consistently delivers non-conforming goods. What action is MOST consistent with ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Immediately terminate the supplier contract to minimize risks.
Increase the frequency of inspections for the incoming goods from this supplier.
Investigate the root cause of the non-conformances and work with the supplier to develop corrective actions.
Accept the non-conformances as part of the risk and cost of doing business.
feedbacks: This is a reactive action and would be ineffective in the longer term.
Inspection is a control not a long term solution.
Investigating and creating corrective actions is the most appropriate response.
This approach is inadequate and not in line with the requirements of the standards.
questions.explanation: Investigating the root cause of non-conformances allows for effective corrective action implementation with the supplier.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'corrective action' in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: To punish those responsible for non-conformities.
To address the immediate effects of a non-conformity.
To prevent the recurrence of non-conformities through root cause analysis.
To improve the documentation process related to the issue.
feedbacks: Corrective actions are not focused on blame.
Immediate actions should come under control not corrective actions.
Root cause analysis and preventive action is the core aim.
Improved documentation is one possible outcome not the aim.
questions.explanation: Corrective action aims to prevent the recurrence of non-conformities by addressing the root cause.

questions.question: When considering 'changes' to the QMS, ISO 9001:2025 requires which of the following?
answers: Changes are not necessary after certification.
Any change should be implemented as soon as possible.
Changes should be planned, controlled, and evaluated for their impact on the QMS.
Changes should be kept secret to avoid confusion.
feedbacks: The QMS should be continually improved.
Changes should be planned and managed.
The standard calls for careful and considered change management.
Changes should be communicated to the necessary parties.
questions.explanation: Changes must be planned, controlled, and evaluated to ensure they do not negatively impact the QMS.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a key element of the 'Plan-Do-Check-Act' (PDCA) cycle used in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Planning of the QMS.
Execution of the plan.
Monitoring the plan.
Marketing the products.
feedbacks: Plan is a core element of the PDCA cycle.
Do is a core element of the PDCA cycle.
Check is a core element of the PDCA cycle.
Marketing is not a core element of PDCA.
questions.explanation: The PDCA cycle covers planning, implementation, assessment, and improvement, not product marketing.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'verification' and 'validation' in the context of ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Verification confirms that the product/service meets the specified requirements, and validation confirms that the process will deliver the intended results.
Verification is focused on validating the process, and validation is focused on the product/service.
Verification and validation are interchangeable terms with identical objectives.
Verification is for internal audits and validation is for external audits.
feedbacks: This represents the correct definition of verification and validation.
This is the incorrect way round.
These are not the same thing.
This is incorrect.
questions.explanation: Verification checks if a product/service meets requirements; validation checks if a process will deliver the required outcome.

questions.question: A company is struggling to meet its quality objectives. According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the most appropriate initial step to rectify this?
answers: Increase employee training, regardless of the issue's root cause.
Re-write procedures that may be unrelated to the issues.
Conduct a thorough analysis to identify the root causes of why the objectives are not being met.
Blame specific employees that may be underperforming.
feedbacks: Training may not be the issue.
Rewrite procedures should be based on analysis.
Root cause analysis is the starting point.
Blaming individuals is not the appropriate response.
questions.explanation: A root cause analysis is required to ensure action is targeted at the underlying cause of the problem.

questions.question: In ISO 9001:2025, the term 'interested parties' primarily refers to:
answers: Governmental regulators, legal experts and other advisors.
The company's shareholders and financial institutions.
All individuals or groups that can affect, be affected by, or believe to be affected by an organization’s decisions or activities.
Employees and senior management only.
feedbacks: These are specific stakeholders but there are more.
Financial stakeholders are also included but there are more.
This is the correct definition of the term.
Employees and senior management are interested parties but the definition is broader.
questions.explanation: Interested parties are those who impact or are impacted by the organization and its QMS.

questions.question: A company's 'quality policy', according to ISO 9001:2025, should:
answers: Be a long and detailed document with specific procedures for every process.
Be kept confidential, to prevent competitors from gaining insights.
Provide a framework for setting quality objectives, be communicated within the organization, and be appropriate to the organization's context.
Be reviewed only during the management review process.
feedbacks: Detailed and prescriptive quality policies are not required.
The quality policy should be communicated internally and externally.
The quality policy defines the commitment to quality and objectives.
The quality policy should be regularly reviewed.
questions.explanation: The quality policy sets the foundation for a QMS, establishing direction and alignment with the organizational context.

questions.question: Which is NOT a typical requirement for 'control of externally provided processes, products and services' according to ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Define criteria for selection and evaluation of external providers.
Ensure clear communication of requirements to the providers.
Regularly assess the performance of the external providers.
Mandate that all external providers must achieve certification to ISO 9001.
feedbacks: This is a fundamental requirement.
Clear communication is required.
Performance assessment is necessary.
ISO 9001 certification is not a mandatory requirement.
questions.explanation: While having certified suppliers is good practice, the standard does not mandate it.

questions.question: A key change in ISO 9001:2025 is the increased focus on which type of risk within a QMS?
answers: Financial risks associated with QMS implementation.
Purely operational risks related to process performance.
Risks associated with potential opportunities to improve the QMS.
Risks that exclusively affect the customer.
feedbacks: While financial risk is a concern, it is not the focus of the change.
Operational risks are important but there is a broader focus.
Identifying and planning for opportunities is a key change.
While customer focused the change has a broader perspective.
questions.explanation: The 2025 update focuses on managing both risks and opportunities as a proactive approach to continuous improvement.

questions.question: How should a company's 'documented information' be managed, according to ISO 9001:2025?
answers: All documentation should be printed and stored in a dedicated physical space.
Access to documentation should be restricted to specific individuals only.
Documentation should be controlled, maintained, and protected, regardless of its format.
Documentation should only be created if specifically requested by an auditor.
feedbacks: Physical documentation is not the only valid form.
Restricting access is not good practice.
This ensures that documentation is always available and up to date.
Documentation should exist to ensure the effective operation of the QMS.
questions.explanation: The standard aims for accessible and maintained documentation regardless of how it is stored and who has access.

questions.question: Which is a key element in the 'performance evaluation' process as required by ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Reliance on qualitative feedback rather than measurable data.
Analysis of the results of monitoring and measurement of key performance indicators.
Auditing of the QMS against the documentation only.
Exclusion of any negative findings to maintain a positive perception of the QMS.
feedbacks: Measurable data is important.
The analysis of data is key to identifying areas of improvement.
Auditing needs to assess the operational performance of the QMS.
All findings both positive and negative must be included in the analysis.
questions.explanation: Performance evaluation involves the analysis of data from KPIs to drive improvement.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, what is the meaning of 'nonconformity'?
answers: A failure to meet customer expectations.
A deviation from a standard or process requirement.
A minor flaw in a single product.
A misunderstanding of the QMS guidelines.
feedbacks: Nonconformity is a broader issue.
This is the correct definition.
Nonconformity applies more broadly to process and systems.
A misunderstanding may be a factor but it is not a nonconformity itself.
questions.explanation: Nonconformity is any deviation from a defined requirement, and is not specific to customer expectations or final product.

questions.question: A company wants to 'demonstrate conformity' to ISO 9001:2025. Which method is MOST suitable?
answers: Self-declaration by the company's CEO.
Internal audits conducted by the company's quality team.
Independent third-party certification.
Providing a certificate of compliance created by the company.
feedbacks: Self-declaration lacks the required level of impartiality.
Internal audits are necessary, but not sufficient for external demonstration.
Third party certification provides the level of assurance required.
Self certification of compliance lacks the required impartiality.
questions.explanation: Independent certification by an accredited certification body provides the most impartial and reliable evidence of conformity.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of the 'improvement' element in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: Maintaining the current processes, without any changes.
Addressing only isolated instances of non-conformity.
Continuously enhancing the effectiveness and suitability of the QMS.
Eliminating all risks, regardless of their likelihood or impact.
feedbacks: This is contrary to the concept of continual improvement.
Improvement requires systemic changes.
This is core focus of the improvement aspect.
Eliminating all risks is not always possible.
questions.explanation: The standard aims for continual improvement and effectiveness of the QMS rather than a state of perfect equilibrium.

questions.question: When considering 'communication' under ISO 9001:2025, what’s the primary focus?
answers: The promotion of products and services to customers.
Ensuring all relevant information about the QMS is effectively shared internally and externally.
Maintaining confidentiality of all QMS information to prevent leaks.
Keeping communication to a bare minimum to prevent overwhelm.
feedbacks: While customer communication is important it is not the only consideration.
Effective communication of the QMS is important.
Confidentiality is not the main focus of communication.
Communication should be effective and timely.
questions.explanation: Effective communication is key to ensuring all interested parties have the necessary information about the QMS.

questions.question: A company identifies a significant opportunity to improve efficiency. According to ISO 9001:2025, what is the recommended approach?
answers: Ignore the opportunity if it is too complex to implement.
Implement the change immediately without formal planning.
Evaluate the opportunity, plan its implementation, and assess its effectiveness.
Postpone implementation of any new ideas.
feedbacks: All opportunities should be explored.
Changes require careful planning and consideration.
This is the most appropriate approach.
All opportunities for improvement should be considered.
questions.explanation: A systematic approach to change includes planning, implementing and evaluating its impact.

questions.question: What is the main objective of the 'management review' process in ISO 9001:2025?
answers: To audit all the processes and systems within the organization.
To conduct an investigation into all internal errors.
To ensure the QMS continues to be suitable, adequate, effective, and aligned with the strategic direction.
To ensure external auditors are satisfied with the company's QMS.
feedbacks: Management review is separate to audit.
Management review should be a positive process.
This is the primary aim.
Management review should benefit the organisation.
questions.explanation: The management review process should help ensure the effectiveness and alignment of the QMS to the business objectives.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, what does 'process approach' mean?
answers: Focusing on individual departments and their specific roles.
Managing all activities as linked processes with inputs and outputs.
Adhering strictly to bureaucratic procedures.
Ignoring the interaction between different business areas.
feedbacks: Process approach considers the whole end to end process.
This is the correct description.
Bureaucracy is not the focus of process approach.
Process approach needs an understanding of the interdependencies of business processes.
questions.explanation: The process approach focuses on managing activities as interconnected processes to deliver an intended result.

questions.question: According to ISO 9001:2025, 'operational planning and control' should ensure which of the following?
answers: Operations are exclusively performed by senior management.
That only legal and regulatory requirements are met.
That processes achieve the planned results, with appropriate controls and monitoring.
That processes are standardized across the entire industry.
feedbacks: This is an incorrect view of operations.
Compliance is a key element but there are other factors.
Effective operation must include monitoring and control.
Industry standardization is not the objective.
questions.explanation: Operational planning ensures effective processes that can deliver planned outcomes while being monitored and controlled.

questions.question: In the context of ISO 9001:2025, 'evidence of conformity' should ideally be:
answers: Based on subjective opinions of stakeholders.
Collected only when requested by an external auditor.
Objective, verifiable, and traceable.
Kept confidential by the QMS manager.
feedbacks: Subjective opinions are not reliable evidence.
